newsitem.title: GERMANY: Major rail routes in Germany sabotaged.
newsitem.headline: Major rail routes in Germany sabotaged.

text.p: Unknown saboteurs brought rail traffic to a near standstill on some of Germany's major routes in a series of incidents early on Monday, a spokesman for German Railways said.

There was no immediate indication who was responsible for the sabotage, the spokesman said, but anti-nuclear activists have tried to block rail traffic several times in the last two years in protest against a nuclear waste dumping ground at Gorleben, 120 km (75 miles) from Hanover, in north Germany.

In Monday's incidents, two trains near Goettingen and two near Hanover ploughed into grappling hooks draped on overhead power cables. One of the trains involved was a high-speed express from Hamburg to Kassel.
Another busy line between Berlin and Magdeburg in the east was also brought to a halt when grappling hooks damaged overhead power lines near Wannsee.
The routes were closed for several hours, delaying tens of thousands of passengers, but no one was injured in the attacks, the spokesman said.
Several hundred trains were re-routed and full service was not restored until Monday afternoon.
Another transport of spent nuclear waste to Gorleben is planned next month.
